title: SIGTERM to a run whose stdout and stderr share one pipe leaves it unsealed at 141; under errexit outside all, a dead stdout ends run_gate at 1
body:
Filed for the weigh of the release after next (vc's todo 214). Record only, with no work now. Laksa's critic review of its runners found it, reading lib/runlog as 0.1.25 ships it; lib/runlog is unchanged at main since v0.1.25.

1. A run whose stdout and stderr both go to a pipe is left unsealed by SIGTERM to its group. When the caller sends both streams to one pipe (`2>&1 | tee`), the signal kills that pipe's reader too. `run_gate` notes the TERM and waits for its command, but before it reaches `trap '' PIPE` (lib/runlog:2432) bash writes the job's "Terminated: 15" notice to the dead stderr, and the shell dies of SIGPIPE. The run exits 141, the in-flight marker stays as the seal, no verdict or ledger row is written, and `$log.progress` is left beside the log. The critic reproduced it 3 of 3 (faithful/r1 to r3-rg-ign-both-TERM: status 141, the .progress file still there). With stderr to a file and only stdout piped, the same signal seals the run red with 143 (faithful/r1-rg-ign-pipe-TERM). The fix to weigh: ignore SIGPIPE from the moment a signal is noted, or before the gated command starts, rather than only after it ends.

2. Lower. `run_gate` called directly under a caller's errexit, outside `all`, exits 1 on the first failed write after a signal, when its stdout has no reader. The seal is written, but the run gets no verdict line, no ledger row, no traps_restore and no re-send of the signal. Under `all`, each gate runs in a subshell and the caller goes on (p1.sh and p2.sh show the two shapes; p4-all.sh and p4-gate.sh, the re-send).

Probes: ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/laksa-critic-probes (copied from the critic's session scratchpad, which dies at reboot).

## Resolution

Fixed by unit 0360-1, landed at 44251731, for 0.1.27 (written 2026-11-17 16:57Z by date -u).

Both faults are closed, and a third the probe found behind the first.

- A signal to the whole group could end the reader of the pipe a run's output goes to. With both streams in one pipe, bash wrote the ended job's notice to that dead stderr before any note ran, and run_gate died of SIGPIPE: 141, the in-flight marker left as the seal, no verdict, no ledger row, the progress file left. run_gate now ignores SIGPIPE in its own shell from just before its pipeline, and each element of the pipeline puts it back at the default for itself, so the gated command, the tee and everything they start keep it as they had it. traps_restore puts the caller's own back with the rest.
- Under a caller's errexit, outside all, the first failed write after a signal to a stdout with no reader ended run_gate at 1, sealed but with no ledger row, no traps_restore and no re-send. errexit now stays off to the close, and the caller's comes back as the run returns.
- Behind the first fix: with both readers gone, each write of the close fails, bash says so on the dead stderr, and BSD stdio keeps those unwritten bytes and writes them again as the shell exits, once the caller's SIGPIPE is back, so the caller still died at 141 after a run that had closed and sent its signal on. The purge, the verdict line and the ledger row are now one helper, run_gate_report, which run_gate runs in a subshell for a run a signal ended, so the failed writes end with it.

Proof: dc's runs on the Desk, 0360-1 stacked with 0359-1 on main c614b4c6.
- The first run (01M7N585NYEGK9KYM80GMJ7JGN, k36s): 0360-1's three arms at its base read the both-streams and errexit arms red and the SIGPIPE control green, as designed; 14 of the 16 files that reach run_gate green whole under BSD and GNU. It found two faults in the stack's own arms, one of them 0360-1's: its control's `yes | head` had no pipe-sound comment, which contract.bats's scan refuses.
- The rerun (01M7N6FT4DDY0ZFBG05PR7MF1C, k36t, at the landed tree 2a02271a): the arms red at the base as before; runlog 140 of 140 and contract 46 of 46 under BSD and GNU; `bin/devbin test scans` 61 of 61; `bin/devbin check lint` 0 breaches.

The records are in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/k36s/runs/ and k36t/runs/.
